observed_result.summary: At the M03-F1 candidate the tests that read the claim table pass on macOS, Linux and Windows, as do the regressions for the review findings: a stored verdict is history (fresh_bind_after_reissue_never_carries_the_stored_claim_values, ensure_data_carries_managed_facts_only_from_this_process_outcome), a client replaced while the effect driver waits claims nothing (client_replaced_while_the_driver_waits_claims_nothing), and on Unix a replaced, removed or unreadable client withholds the claims until verified again (replaced_client_withholds_the_claims_until_verified_again). On each host the observation reads the claim platform, the OS release and the selected client, and the real table applies exactly that platform's entries: 7 on macOS 27.2.1 with 10.5p1 and on Linux 6.8.0-147-generic with 9.6p1, 5 on Windows 10.0.26300.9974 with the in-box 9.5p2 (no owned_multiplexing, no graceful_dedicated_connections). The whole Linux workspace suite passed at this commit.

limitations: Targeted reruns on macOS and Windows (ADR-0009 section 2 item 2); check.sh ran on macOS at this commit (3427 passed, 0 failed, 199 ignored); the whole workspace ran on Linux.

No WSL run, by the orchestrator's ruling: under WSL the claim platform is `wsl` when a marker shows, and otherwise a WSL kernel is not a native release of the Linux floor's flavour; the domain and localenv unit tests cover both on every platform.
The OS floors extend upward by ADR-0008 D12's design (m03-exit.md section 3 item 20): a later release of the same flavour with the same pinned client and signer build is covered without its own run.
Debug test-configured builds: no entry is a custody claim (ADR-0008 D12 item 3, F03); lock_continuity stays not_verified.
The client-replacement, read-denial and FIFO tests are Unix-only; on Windows the identity is the opened handle's (GetFileInformationByHandle) and the registry reader's checks are unit-tested.
The Windows logs are redacted: the scratch checkout reads <scratch> and the Windows home <home>. The Windows run's commit is as reported by the orchestrator's agent.
